best_for: People with two or three computers on one desk, say a work laptop and a home PC, who want one keyboard and mouse for all of them without buying a hardware switch.

points.title: A software KVM, minus the video
points.text: Move the pointer off the edge of one screen and it lands on the next computer, with the keyboard following. Each machine keeps its own monitor.

points.title: Copy here, paste there
points.text: The clipboard is shared between machines. Version 1.27.0 added clipboard support on Wayland through desktop portals.

points.title: The open upstream of Synergy
points.text: Deskflow began as Synergy in 2001 and is free under GPL-2.0. It talks to Synergy 1, Input Leap and Barrier on the network, but not to Synergy 3. Synergy, the commercial fork, sponsors the project.

points.title: Encrypted by default
points.text: Traffic between computers uses TLS out of the box, so keystrokes do not cross your network in plain text.

points.title: Wayland still has gaps
points.text: Wayland works through libei and libportal, but the project warns some features may be missing or broken there. Windows needs Windows 10 version 1809 or later and the Visual C++ Redistributable.

points.title: Mac builds come from elsewhere
points.text: Deskflow runs on macOS too, but this site lists only Windows and Linux. Mac users get it from the project's GitHub releases or Homebrew.

points.title: What is listed here
points.text: Windows MSI installers for x64 and Arm64 install for all users, and the Windows listing keeps 16 versions. The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub, so it comes from the Deskflow developers; only its current release is listed, so a downgrade needs another source.
